# LOADING PACKAGES.
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
rm(list = ls())
library(tidyverse)
library(peRspective)
theme_set(theme_bw() + theme(text = element_text(size = 15)))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# LOAD IN DATA.
```{r LOAD IN DATA}
# Create dataframe "data" which contains cleaned participant data without pure controls.
data <- read_csv('../Data/original_posts_scored.csv') #read csv data file.
```


# FORMAT DATA.
```{r FORMAT DATA}
# compute humility score as average of 3 perspective scores
data <- data %>% mutate(humility = (nuance + curiosity + respect) / 3)
```

# COMPARE HUMBLE AND NOT HUMBLE POSTS
```{r COMPARE HUMBLE AND NOT HUMBLE POSTS}

# Cohen's d with pooled SD (classic, equal-variance pooling)
cohen_d <- function(x, y) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]; y <- y[!is.na(y)]
  nx <- length(x); ny <- length(y)
  sp <- sqrt(((nx - 1) * var(x) + (ny - 1) * var(y)) / (nx + ny - 2))
  (mean(x) - mean(y)) / sp
}
 

y_hi <- data[data$High_IH == "Yes", ]$humility
y_no <- data[data$High_IH == "No", ]$humility
tt <- t.test(y_hi, y_no)               # Welch's t-test (unequal variances)
results <- data.frame(
  outcome = 'humility',
  n_yes   = sum(!is.na(y_hi)),
  n_no    = sum(!is.na(y_no)),
  mean_yes = mean(y_hi, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean_no  = mean(y_no, na.rm = TRUE),
  d  = cohen_d(y_hi, y_no),
  t  = unname(tt$statistic),
  df = unname(tt$parameter),
  p  = tt$p.value
)

cat('High IH posts had an average humility rating of', round(results$mean_yes, 3), 'while the remaining posts had an average humility rating of', round(results$mean_no, 3), 
'. Results were statistically significantly different according to a Welch\'s two-sample',
't-test ($d = ', 
        round(results$d, 3), 
        ', t = ', 
        round(results$t, 3), 
        ', df = ', 
        round(results$df, 3),
        ', P < 0.001.$)'
)
 

```
